title: Client degradation sentinel & tool-graph PRD (ideation)
content:
Summary:

This is an ideation-stage PRD for a small-surface change to the Hosted API that aims to make client-visible degradation predictable and manageable when tool-calls, structured outputs, or streaming paths fail or slow. The guiding principle: never leave a developer app with silent stalls or confusing partial outputs — provide a deterministic, inspectable sentinel and a graph model for tool resolution so clients can make simple decisions (retry, degrade, present partial UI).

Why this exists (problem):
- Customers build interactive UIs and rely on partial streaming output + ad-hoc tool calls. When tool backends are slow or model fallbacks trigger, the client often blocks waiting for a final event.
- Current hosted streaming provides deltas but no first-class marker describing degraded state or tool-graph resolution status. Developers add brittle heuristics in SDKs/UI.
- We need a repeatable contract that supports: progressive partials, tool-call graph summaries, and clear sentinel events indicating graceful degradation, fallback, or retry windows.

Goals (MVP):
- Define a small, versioned sentinel event (text enum + metadata) that appears in streaming responses and final response envelopes to indicate operational state: OK, SOFT_DEGRADE, HARD_DEGRADE, TOOL_PENDING, TOOL_FAILED, FALLBACK_USED.
- Attach a compact tool-graph snapshot to the response envelope when any tool calls are made. The snapshot should explain which tools were attempted, their latency profile, and resolution (succeeded/failed/aborted/queued).
- Surface a light client SDK abstraction that exposes sentinel events via callbacks/promises and gives a small set of actionable flags for UI (show spinner, show partial, show degraded banner, allow retry).
- Keep token/response overhead minimal (tool-graph summary limited to N entries).

Non-goals (MVP):
- Full fidelity per-tool logs (those stay in Console/tracing).
- Complex client-side orchestration libraries (we ship ergonomic primitives only).

Constraints and assumptions:
- We must preserve existing streaming wire semantics for backwards compatibility; older clients should ignore sentinel fields.
- Sentinel and graph must be serializable in current streaming frames (compact JSON or newline-delimited small object).
- Avoid exposing secrets or internal identifiers for external services; tool entries use opaque ids and public-friendly names.

Proposed sentinel contract (high-level):
- sentinel: { version: "v1", state: "OK" | "SOFT_DEGRADE" | "HARD_DEGRADE" | "TOOL_PENDING" | "TOOL_FAILED" | "FALLBACK_USED", reason: string, suggested_action: "wait" | "present_partial" | "retry" | "none", retry_window_ms?: number }
- This object appears as a special streaming frame (frame_type: "sentinel") and as a top-level field in final JSON responses for sync calls.
- Example sentinel in-stream: { version: "v1", state: "TOOL_PENDING", reason: "external-tool/ocr slow", suggested_action: "present_partial", retry_window_ms: 8000 }

Tool-graph snapshot (summary):
- Flat list of tool nodes limited to first 6 nodes to bound size. Each node: { id: "t_0x12", name: "ocr-service", attempt: 1, status: "pending"|"ok"|"failed"|"aborted", latency_ms_estimate: 1200 }
- The graph does not include full DAG edges in MVP; we include a topological order list and a small edge hint field for simple chains.
- Example summary (as stringified JSON in frame): [{"id":"t1","name":"extract_text","status":"ok","latency_ms":230},{"id":"t2","name":"format_resume","status":"failed","latency_ms":1200}]

SDK ergonomics (developer-facing):
- Add two new callbacks on streaming client: onSentinel(sentinelObj) and onToolGraph(toolList). These are optional and default no-op.
- For promise-based APIs, final response includes sentinel + tool_graph fields.
- Provide a small helper: sentinelActionMapper(sentinelObj) -> { uiState: "spinner"|"partial"|"degradedBanner", showRetryButton: bool, retryInMs: number | null }
- Keep the SDK changes tiny (single new module). We want to reduce adoption friction.

Streaming wire details (notes to eng):
- Introduce frame_type = "sentinel" and frame_type = "tool_graph". Both are small JSON blobs. They are non-blocking frames; clients may receive them interleaved with token frames.
- Backwards compatibility: clients that don't recognize the frame type should ignore (we must document this explicitly).
- Frames must be produced within 10ms of state change to be actionable.

Structured output & partials (application UX):
- When a tool is pending, server should emit a partial structured token if available and then emit a sentinel with suggested_action: "present_partial". Example: structured partial could be a best-effort JSON summary of extracted fields.
- Final responses should include structured_output_v1 and sentinel fields. structured_output_v1 is the canonical shape for downstream evaluation and should be stable.

Fallback policies (runtime):
- If primary tool call latency > threshold T_soft (default 1.5s), emit SOFT_DEGRADE sentinel and optional partials.
- If latency exceeds T_hard (default 5s) or tool returns clear failure, mark TOOL_FAILED and either use a fallback model or return FALLBACK_USED depending on availability.
- Fallback decisions happen server-side; sentinel communicates final decision and the chosen fallback.

Telemetry & metrics (for rollout):
- Track sentinel emissions per model/route: sentinel.rate, median time to first sentinel, distribution of suggested_action.
- Tool-graph telemetry stored in Console/traces; summarized counts emitted to product metrics: percent_tool_pending, percent_tool_failed, percent_fallback_used.
- Uplift: build dashboard to correlate sentinel types with user-visible error reports (DSAT).

Rollout plan (phases):
- Alpha: internal SDK + a small set of customers in beta (2–3) — opt-in flag. Collect telemetry and integration notes.
- Beta: broader opt-in, SDK stable, console dashboards for sentinel rates.
- GA: enabled by default with config to toggle sentinel verbosity and tool-graph size.

Open design questions / TODOs (engineering + product):
- Should we include a minimal edge description (edges) in the tool-graph MVP or avoid complexity? (engineering leans minimal)
- Exact size cap per tool-graph frame and effect of very large graphs on mobile clients.
- Backwards compatibility testing matrix: old SDKs vs new server frames — need fuzz tests.
- UX patterns: what do common customer apps do when they receive SOFT_DEGRADE? (question for solutions eng to gather examples).

Quick integration notes for Solutions/SDKs:
- Provide a small sample in the quickstart: "how to show a degraded banner and a retry button using onSentinel".
- Example (pseudocode):
  client.onSentinel = s => { const action = sentinelActionMapper(s); if (action.uiState === 'partial') renderPartial(snapshot); if (action.showRetryButton) showRetry(action.retryInMs); }

References & links:
- See linked PR / runtime spec for streaming frame change (github above).
- Related tickets: JIRA-API-847 (tool-call telemetry), CONFLUENCE-1482 (UX playbook).

Next steps (owner: Avery):
- Align with runtime on frame format and size cap (due 2025-09-05).
- Ship internal alpha SDK and coordinate with 2 solutions-eng customers for an integration test (target 2025-09-30).
- Draft Console dashboard wire and metrics contract (with observability team).

Notes to self:
- Keep language simple in docs: developer should be able to reason about sentinel enum in < 1 minute.
- Do not leak internal hostnames or run ids in tool-graph. Use opaque short ids.

---
End of ideation PRD draft.
